ai.purpose: Define the TEL (Triadic Expression Layer) system — the formal grammar by which structures express, encode, represent, and transform meaning. Introduces TEL operators (TEL-Σ, TEL-Ε, TEL-Κ, TEL-Τ, TEL-Α), syntax maps, semantic maps, composition rules, and phase cycles. TEL is the expressive engine of the TriadicFrameworks canon.
ai.summary: Book 5 formalizes the Triadic Expression Layer (TEL), defining how structures encode and express meaning. It introduces the five TEL operators, the syntax and semantic maps, the composition grammar, and the six-phase evaluation cycle. TEL is the expressive counterpart to Book 3’s detection grammar and is required for all downstream reasoning in Books 7, 8, and 9.

references: INV-TEL-001: Expression Validity — an expression is valid only if its syntax tree conforms to the TEL syntax map.
INV-TEL-002: Semantic Coherence — semantic evaluation must produce a coherent meaning state under TEL-Ε.
INV-TEL-003: Composition Integrity — TEL compositions must preserve operator roles and structural constraints.
INV-TEL-004: Assertion Closure — TEL-Α assertions must remain closed under the TEL evaluation cycle.
